record.original_question: For a fixed(finitely generated free)-by-cyclic group G = Fn ⋊ Z, is there an algorithm that, given a finite subset S of G, finds a finite presentation for the subgroup H = ⟨S⟩? Cf. 4.8 in Archive.

evidence.quote: For a fixed(finitely generated free)-by-cyclic group G = Fn ⋊ Z, is there an algorithm that, given a finite subset S of G, finds a finite presentation for the subgroup H = ⟨S⟩? Cf. 4.8 in Archive.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $F_n$ denote the free group of rank $n \geq 2$, and let $G = F_n \rtimes_\varphi \mathbb{Z}$ be a (finitely generated free)-by-cyclic group, where $\varphi \in \mathrm{Aut}(F_n)$ specifies the action of the generator of $\mathbb{Z}$ on $F_n$. Fix such a group $G$ (with $n$ and $\varphi$ given). It is known that every finitely generated subgroup $H \leq G$ is finitely presented.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm which, given as input a finite subset $S \subset G$ (with elements expressed as words in fixed generators of $G$), outputs a finite presentation $\langle X \mid R \rangle$ of the subgroup $H = \langle S \rangle$ generated by $S$?
artifact.status_search_result: Feighn–Handel established that finitely generated subgroups of free-by-cyclic groups are finitely presented, but this proof is not effective. The algorithmic question of computing such a finite presentation from a generating set is listed as a new problem in the Kourovka Notebook and we found no published algorithm resolving it; thus it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Virtually Free-by-Cyclic Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Background on finiteness properties of subgroups of free-by-cyclic groups, citing Feighn–Handel finite presentability.
status_evidence.claim: Finitely generated subgroups of free-by-cyclic groups are finitely presented (existence result), but effective computation of such presentations is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Free-by-cyclic group - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Lists known algorithmic results (word problem, conjugacy problem solvable) for free-by-cyclic groups; no algorithm given for computing presentations of arbitrary finitely generated subgroups.
status_evidence.claim: No algorithm is known in the literature for computing finite presentations of arbitrary finitely generated subgroups of a free-by-cyclic group.
